The week strip is story 1, at the week story 1 describes: today is Thursday the 17th, cycle day 4, the three days behind it are period days, and the 18th is predicted. A period day is a filled circle, today is ringed, and a predicted day is a dotted outline.
The map draws no fill, no ring and no dotted outline, so the line under the strip names the state of every day. That line is not a row on the phone.
The phase line, the ring and the forecast all read day 4 of a 31 day cycle that started on the 14th of September.
The line under the strip is story 2. The phase word takes the ink partner of its phase and never sits on the phase fill, which is SEE-2.
Two round actions, period and symptoms, which is the decision the operator took in section 12 of the stories.
The body of this screen is four more frames in the map, because the map draws one frame at a time and this screen scrolls. No link stands for the scroll: a scroll is not a press.
defects: The week strip, the phase line and the round actions are all new. The screen today carries none of them.

Stories 9 and 10 both start here and both need the calendar, and this screen opens no calendar. Where she opens it is undecided. The header carries the mark, the word and the greeting only, the dock holds four columns already, and no third place is drawn.

Story 2 asks for a line that reads across a room, and SCREEN-2 refuses the word period above 14 points on this screen. The drawing gives the size to the day number and holds the phase word small. Is that the answer, or does the phase word change?

stories.steps: One answer in the first run, then one press two days before.
stories.story: She reaches the reminder screen in the first run and turns the reminder on. Two days before the forecast start, her phone shows a notification. She presses it and Emi opens on the log. Nothing about a period is sent anywhere for this to work: the phone holds the forecast, so the phone schedules the notification.
stories.title: Story 11: Emi tells her the period is near, and her phone alone raises it

edges: Done, and the month draws the change
A day that has not happened
lanes: The month, and a day in it
A day Emi refuses
stories.steps: Four presses from the screen she opens to a day two months back.
stories.story: She presses the calendar. She reads September. She swipes back to August. She presses the 14th, reads what she wrote and edits it. A day that has not happened is refused in the words the address already refuses it in.
stories.title: Story 9: She opens a month and reads any day in it

edges: Back, and the ring has moved
One day, the only way that exists today
lanes: The whole period at once
One day at a time, which is what exists
stories.steps: Two presses in, one save, and the ring has moved.
stories.story: She presses Edit my period. The month opens with the period Emi holds drawn on it. She adds two days, removes one, and saves once. Every day of the range becomes a day record whose revision rises, and the cycle cache is rebuilt from the day log rather than written by hand.
stories.title: Story 10: She corrects a whole period in one action

edges: Today, and the forecast has moved
lanes: Correcting an answer
The two ways out that already exist
stories.steps: Three presses to the answer, one save.
stories.story: She opens Privacy. She presses her cycle length. She moves it from 28 to 31 and saves. The forecast on the screen she opens has moved. The profile stays one sealed row, and this screen writes it through the envelope the first run used.
stories.title: Story 12: She changes an answer she gave at the first run

lanes: What she opens
stories.steps: No press at all. She opens Emi and reads.
stories.story: She opens Emi. The strip is the first thing under the wordmark. She reads that today is day 21, that the days behind it carry their own cycle day, and which day is predicted. She presses nothing.
stories.title: Story 1: She reads her week without opening anything

edges: The same line, three weeks later
Back to the week she opens
lanes: The line she opens on, in her period
The same line, in the luteal phase
stories.steps: No press at all. She reads it from across the room.
stories.story: She opens Emi. Under the strip she reads one line that names the phase and the day, and she reads it from where she left the phone. The line never sits on a phase fill: three of the four phase colours fail the contrast floor as text, so the line takes the ink partner of its phase.
stories.title: Story 2: She reads what day of her cycle she is on, in words

edges: Press what you logged to change it
lanes: Symptoms, in two presses
The flow, in two presses
stories.steps: Two presses from opening Emi to a symptom recorded.
stories.story: She opens Emi. She presses the round action for symptoms. The log opens on the symptom groups. She marks two symptoms and saves. She returns to the screen she started on and the symptoms are on it. Two round actions, period and symptoms, which is the decision the operator took.
stories.title: Story 3: She starts a log in one press, from the screen she opens

lanes: The three numbers, and where they are measured against
stories.steps: One scroll, and one press to the papers.
stories.story: She opens Emi and scrolls once. She reads that her last cycle ran 37 days, that her last period ran 7 days, and how much her cycles vary. Beside each number she reads the published figure and she reaches the paper from that screen. No row calls a woman abnormal.
stories.title: Story 4: She reads her own three cycle numbers, beside a published range

edges: A cycle row opens the day it started
lanes: The strips, and the screen that already draws them
stories.steps: Two scrolls, one press out and one press back.
stories.story: She opens Emi and scrolls. She reads the current cycle and the two before it, each as a strip. She presses one and lands on Insights at that cycle, and she comes back. The strips read the cycle cache, so the arithmetic is not written twice.
stories.title: Story 6: She sees each past cycle as a strip, on the screen she opens

edges: The same six cycles, in full
lanes: The chart, and the numbers it must agree with
stories.story: She opens Emi and scrolls. She reads the six points, the band behind them, and one sentence that counts how many fell outside it. Nothing is drawn before two complete cycles exist.
stories.title: Story 5: She reads the shape of her last six cycles

edges: The card opens the pattern in full
lanes: The card, and the screen it agrees with
stories.story: She opens Emi and scrolls. She reads that bloating came back on day 12 in four of her last six cycles. She presses the card and reads the whole pattern on Insights. A symptom logged once or twice is never named a pattern, and no card compares her with another woman.
stories.title: Story 7: She meets the symptom that comes back, without going to look for it

edges: Done, and the sections have arrived
Start again, on a fresh phone
lanes: Day one
After her first period
stories.steps: Two scrolls on day one, one log, and the screen fills in.
stories.story: She finishes the first run and opens Emi. Where a section needs two cycles and she has none, she reads one sentence that says what it needs and when it arrives. She does not read an empty chart and she never reads sample data. She logs one period, opens Emi again, and the sections her data now supports have arrived.
stories.title: Story 8: A section she has not earned is absent, and she is told why

edges: Done, through the rest of the questions
lanes: The first run, without a date
The screen she opens, and the day she logs
stories.steps: One press past the one question she cannot answer.
stories.story: She reaches the last period question, presses I do not remember, and Emi takes her on. The screen she opens carries no ring, and it says the first period she logs starts everything. Emi builds no forecast from a guessed date.
stories.title: Story 13: She starts Emi without remembering when her last period started

dataModel.intro: Four tables on the phone and one in the cloud. Two of the four hold ciphertext and nothing else. The server holds an encrypted vault and no key, so no story below can be served by reading a row on it.

zones.sub: SQLite, opened with a key that is made on the phone and kept in the keychain.
zones.title: On the phone

tables.name: day_log
tables.role: One row for one day. A trigger refuses a write that does not raise the revision.
fields: when she first wrote the day

tables.name: cycle
tables.role: The cache the ring, the forecast, the strips and the chart all read. Every value is derived from day_log, so it carries no revision and no sync marker.
fields: nothing at all while it runs

tables.name: setting
tables.role: A key and a value, in plain text, for the things that are not about her body. The reminder of story 11 belongs here.

tables.name: profile
tables.role: Exactly one row, holding the eight answers the first run sealed. Story 12 writes this row through the envelope the first run used, and adds no second copy of any answer.

zones.sub: DynamoDB. No attribute carries a date, a symptom, a flow or a note.
zones.title: On the server

tables.name: emi-vault
tables.role: The account and the record items. The service reads ciphertext and holds no key that opens it.
fields: the public key of the phone
refused when it does not rise

decisions: Story 4 wants a published range beside her own cycle length. The code cites a bound for the period duration and a figure for the cycle length variation, and it cites nothing for the cycle length range. Which published range does that row sit against?
Story 11 puts two values in the setting table in plain text: how many days before, and the time of day. Neither is about her body. Is plain text right for both?
Story 10 rewrites a range of day records in one action. Every day in the range raises its own revision, so one save can push six records to the server. Is that one request or six?
